Container.Name: loglook
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: loglook syslog log viewer unraid syslog server read-only api tokens n8n
Container.Overview:
Small read-only viewer and API for the syslog files Unraid's built-in syslog server collects (syslog-IP.log and its rotated copies). Pick a device and a time window and loglook finds the lines by their own timestamps across the live and rotated files, so you never open a multi-gigabyte file by hand.
Three views of any window: the lines, top patterns (MACs, IPs and numbers collapsed so repeats become one row with a count) and counts per captured value. Filters take plain text or a regex, and a window can end earlier to compare today with previous days. A read-only JSON API behind bearer tokens serves the same queries to scripts and automations such as n8n. Tokens are created in the web UI, shown once, and stored hashed.
Setup: set Syslog Folder to your Unraid syslog share (Settings, Syslog Server, Local syslog folder). Create sources.yml in the Config folder to name each device by IP (an example is in the project README, https://github.com/ccmpbll/loglook/blob/main/sources.example.yml); without it every device shows as unmapped. Open the web UI and create the admin user on first run. The log folder is mounted read-only and nothing in it is ever changed.
Web interface: http://UNRAID_IP:8000

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the web interface and the API.

Config.Name: Syslog Folder
Config.Description: The folder your syslog server writes to (files named syslog-IP.log). Mounted read-only.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Put sources.yml here: which IP is which device, and optionally how long silence is worth flagging. Without it every device shows as unmapped.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: The admin login, API tokens and the generated session key. Keep on persistent storage.

Config.Name: Secret Key
Config.Description: Optional. Signs the login cookie. Leave empty and a random key is generated on first start and kept in the Data folder.

Config.Name: Secure Cookies
Config.Description: Set to true only when you reach loglook over HTTPS (a reverse proxy such as Traefik terminates TLS). The login does not work over plain HTTP while this is on.
